step1_summary: Chief complaint: Sudden onset severe left-sided headache noted on awakening this morning.

Symptoms: • Onset ~05:30 today, woke patient from sleep. • Constant, unilateral (left) head pain, described as worse than any prior headache. • Mild photophobia. • Initial dizziness that resolved. • No neck stiffness, no fever, no nausea/vomiting. • Slightly better after lying down for a while; paracetamol provided no relief.
Past medical history: Generalised anxiety disorder (≈2 yrs). Intermittent, less-severe frontal ‘cluster’-type headaches in the past. No hypertension or other chronic conditions.
Medications / allergies: Takes sertraline chronically; single dose of paracetamol today. No known drug allergies.

Family / social history: Mother with anxiety; no family history of migraine or other significant disease. Lives with partner, non-smoker, runs 3×/week, average diet, owns a cat. Work stress and late nights for ≈2 months.
Vital signs / exam: Telephone consult – no vitals or physical-exam findings available. Patient denies focal neurologic deficits.
Labs / imaging: None performed or reported.

V: Subarachnoid haemorrhage: sudden severe unilateral headache that awakened patient from sleep could represent ‘thunderclap’ bleed.
Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis: acute persistent headache; risk factors unknown but presentation can mimic migraine.
I: Viral or bacterial meningitis: acute headache, photophobia; however lacks fever/neck stiffness.
Acute sinusitis (frontal/ethmoid): unilateral/frontal pain worsened early morning, mild photophobia.
N: Intracranial mass/brain tumour: new, progressively worse unilateral headache, early-morning pain, poor response to simple analgesia.
D: Tension-type headache: stress-related, bilateral or band-like pain that can become unilateral, associated with prolonged work stress.
Cervicogenic/musculoskeletal headache: posture-related from long hours, improved by lying down.
I2: Medication-overuse headache: frequent paracetamol or other analgesic use can worsen headaches, though only single dose reported today.
Sertraline-induced headache: SSRI can cause headaches as adverse effect.
C: Arteriovenous malformation: congenital vascular lesion that can present with sudden severe headache if bleeding.
A: Temporal (giant-cell) arteritis: unilateral headache; unlikely at age 39 but autoimmune consideration.
T: Post-traumatic headache: typically follows head injury—none reported.
E: Migraine (endocrine/metabolic/neurovascular): unilateral throbbing pain, photophobia, stress/sleep deprivation trigger.
Hypertensive crisis: severe headache, early morning; no BP known.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Unilateral severe headache, photophobia, past intermittent headaches, stress/sleep deprivation as trigger, normal neuro screen, and age all favour migraine.
History of anxiety, sustained work stress, prior similar but milder headaches, bilateral turned unilateral possible; absence of nausea or neurological signs fits tension component.
Early-morning awakening, strictly unilateral severe pain, male in typical age group; however lacks autonomic features and orbital localisation.
Sudden onset severe headache that woke patient from sleep could represent thunderclap bleed; seriousness mandates consideration despite paucity of other findings.
New, increasingly severe unilateral headaches worse in early morning and unresponsive to simple analgesia can herald tumour, although single-day history argues against.

supporting_evidence: Stress and sleep deprivation are common migraine triggers

opposing_evidence: Current pain is unilateral and more severe than typical tension headache
Presence of photophobia (less common in tension headaches)

supporting_evidence: Awoke patient in early morning (circadian pattern typical)
opposing_evidence: Absence of autonomic features (tearing, rhinorrhoea, ptosis)
Headache continuous rather than brief paroxysms

supporting_evidence: Acute severe headache waking patient from sleep
Described as worse than previous headaches
opposing_evidence: No thunderclap description, gradual onset implied
No neck stiffness, photophobia minimal, neurologic deficits absent
Normal consciousness and conversation hours later

supporting_evidence: Worse headache than usual, unilateral, early-morning pain (possible raised ICP pattern)
opposing_evidence: Only one-day history; tumours usually cause progressive symptoms over weeks–months
No neurological focal deficits or vomiting
